summary: The `next lint` command is deprecated (warns, removed in 16); projects should run ESLint or Biome directly instead of `next lint`.
The `legacyBehavior` prop of `next/link` (child `<a>` wrapper mode) is deprecated with a warning; use `<Link>` without a child anchor instead.
Built-in AMP support (`useAmp` from `next/amp`, page `config.amp`, the `amp` next.config key) is deprecated with a warning ahead of removal in 16.
`next/image` now warns when a `quality` other than 75 is used while `images.qualities` is unset, because 16 will restrict qualities to the configured list.
`next/image` now warns when a local `src` carries a query string while `images.localPatterns` is unset, because 16 will require a matching localPatterns entry.
`unstable_rootParams` (from `next/server`) is deprecated with a warning; the replacement is the `next/root-params` module.
Config keys renamed with auto-migration of the old name: `experimental.typedRoutes` becomes top-level `typedRoutes` (now stable), and `experimental.dynamicIO` becomes `experimental.cacheComponents`.
The exported `NextRequest` type no longer exposes Next.js-internal members; code that typed against those internals no longer compiles.
`serverRuntimeConfig` / `publicRuntimeConfig` in next.config (read via `getConfig()` from `next/config`) now log a deprecation warning; environment variables are the replacement.
Minimum supported versions raised: Node.js 20.9.0 (18.x no longer supported; engines field changed) and TypeScript 5.1.0.
The default browserslist targets moved to Baseline widely-available browsers (Chrome/Edge/Firefox 111+, Safari 16.4+), changing the JS/CSS output for projects without their own browserslist.
`next dev`, `next build` and custom servers now use Turbopack by default instead of webpack; `--turbopack` is unnecessary, `--webpack` opts out, and a build with a `webpack` config and no flag fails.
When a Babel config file is present, Turbopack now enables Babel automatically instead of exiting with a hard error.
The deprecated `experimental.turbo` config object is removed; Turbopack options must live under the top-level `turbopack` key.

Turbopack config keys moved: `experimental.turbopackPersistentCaching` is replaced by `experimental.turbopackFileSystemCacheForDev`/`ForBuild`, and `turbopack.moduleIds` becomes `experimental.turbopackModuleIds`.
The temporary synchronous access to `cookies()`, `headers()`, `draftMode()` and to the `params`/`searchParams` props kept for 15 is removed; these are Promises and must be awaited.

Metadata route functions receive Promises instead of plain values: image generators (`opengraph-image`, `twitter-image`, `icon`, `apple-icon`) get `params` and `id` as Promises, and `sitemap` gets `id` as a Promise.
Config keys moved out of `experimental` to the top level (old location deprecated): `reactCompiler`, `cacheComponents`, `cacheLife` profiles and `cacheHandlers`.
The `experimental.dynamicIO` and `experimental.useCache` flags are removed; the behavior is enabled with top-level `cacheComponents: true`.

Partial Prerendering config is removed: `experimental.ppr` (including `'incremental'`) and the route-level `export const experimental_ppr` are no longer accepted; PPR is opted into via `cacheComponents`.
`unstable_cacheLife` and `unstable_cacheTag` from `next/cache` are stabilized as `cacheLife` and `cacheTag` (the old names are still accepted but are no longer the documented imports).

`revalidateTag(tag)` now requires a second `cacheLife` profile argument (e.g. `'max'`) for stale-while-revalidate; the single-argument form is deprecated and is a TypeScript error, with `updateTag(tag)` for immediate expiry.

The new router/prefetch implementation (`experimental.clientSegmentCache`) is on by default: prefetches are per segment with layout deduplication and incremental fetching, so navigations issue more, smaller requests.
The `middleware` file convention and `middleware` export are deprecated in favor of `proxy.ts` exporting `proxy`, which runs only on the Node.js runtime (keep `middleware` for the Edge runtime).

middleware-named APIs renamed to proxy (old names kept as deprecated aliases): `skipMiddlewareUrlNormalize`->`skipProxyUrlNormalize`, `experimental.middlewarePrefetch`->`proxyPrefetch`, `experimental.externalMiddlewareRewritesResolve`->`externalProxyRewritesResolve`, types `NextMiddleware`->`NextProxy`, `MiddlewareConfig`->`ProxyConfig`, `MiddlewareMatcher`->`ProxyMatcher`, and `onRequestError` context `routeType` `'middleware'`->`'proxy'`.
A local `next/image` `src` with a query string now needs a matching `images.localPatterns` entry (with `search`); previously any query string was optimized.
`images.minimumCacheTTL` default changed from 60 seconds to 14400 seconds (4 hours) for optimized images without cache-control headers.
`images.imageSizes` default no longer includes 16, so `next/image` srcsets stop offering a 16px candidate unless configured.
`images.qualities` default changed from allowing 1-100 to `[75]`; a `quality` prop is coerced to the closest configured value and other `q` values on `/_next/image` return 400.
The image optimizer now refuses to fetch from local/private IP addresses by default; `images.dangerouslyAllowLocalIP: true` restores the old behavior.
`images.maximumRedirects` default changed from unlimited to 3 redirects when fetching remote images.
The `next/legacy/image` component is deprecated with a warning; use `next/image`.
The `images.domains` config is deprecated with a warning; use `images.remotePatterns`.
`next dev` now writes to `.next/dev` (including generated types) instead of sharing `.next` with `next build`, so dev and build can run concurrently.
`next dev` and `next build` now acquire a lockfile on the dist directory, so a second `next dev` or `next build` on the same project fails instead of running.
Parallel route slots with routable children now require an explicit `default.js`; the build fails instead of silently 404ing at runtime.
`@next/eslint-plugin-next` and `eslint-config-next` now default to ESLint flat config; the legacy `.eslintrc` `extends: 'next'` form is no longer supported at v16.
The router no longer temporarily resets a global `scroll-behavior: smooth` during navigations; add `data-scroll-behavior="smooth"` on `<html>` to get the old override back.
`next build` output no longer prints the `Size` and `First Load JS` columns per route (and the manifests behind them are gone).
`next dev` loads next.config only in the server process, so `process.argv` inside the config no longer contains `'dev'`; use `NODE_ENV` or the config `phase` instead.
sass-loader is bumped to v16, which uses the modern Sass JS API; legacy-API `sassOptions` and the silenced legacy deprecation no longer apply.
Built-in AMP support is removed: `useAmp`/`next/amp`, page `config.amp` and the `amp` next.config key no longer exist.
The `next lint` command is removed, `next build` no longer runs ESLint, and the `eslint` key in next.config is no longer supported; run ESLint or Biome directly.
`serverRuntimeConfig` and `publicRuntimeConfig` (and `getConfig()` from `next/config`) are removed; use environment variables (`NEXT_PUBLIC_` for client values).
The `devIndicators` options `appIsrStatus`, `buildActivity` and `buildActivityPosition` are removed (the indicator itself remains).
`unstable_rootParams` is removed; use the `next/root-params` module.
The `NextConfig` type no longer extends `Record<string, any>`, so unknown or misspelled keys in a typed `next.config.ts` are now TypeScript errors.
The `experimental.clientSegmentCache` config key is removed; the segment cache router cannot be turned off any more.
Turbopack filesystem caching for `next dev` (`experimental.turbopackFileSystemCacheForDev`) is now on by default, persisting compiler artifacts under `.next` between runs.
`next build` now fails for App Router paths that normalize to the same route (e.g. `[slug]` vs `[modalSlug]` siblings) instead of letting the conflict surface at runtime.

In a `'use cache'` module, re-exports and exports of non-literal values (e.g. `export { getData } from`, `export const x = fn`) are now wrapped as cache functions at runtime, where previously only directly declared functions were.
The image optimizer's on-disk cache is now an LRU bounded by the new `images.maximumDiskCacheSize` (default: 50% of available disk space) instead of growing without limit.

Server Action CSRF validation now treats `Origin: null` (sandboxed iframes and other opaque contexts) as an explicit cross-origin value and rejects it unless `'null'` is listed in `experimental.serverActions.allowedOrigins`; it was previously treated as a missing origin and allowed.
`experimental.adapterPath` (Build Adapters) is promoted to the top-level `adapterPath` config key; the experimental location is deprecated.

`experimental.browserDebugInfoInTerminal` is replaced by `logging.browserToTerminal` (`boolean | 'error' | 'warn'`); the object form with `depthLimit`/`edgeLimit`/`showSourceLocation` is gone and the old key warns.
In development, browser `console.error`/`console.warn` output is now forwarded to the terminal by default (level `'warn'`) instead of only when opted in.
The image optimizer now rejects source images whose response body exceeds the new `images.maximumResponseBody` (default 50 MB), where previously any size was accepted.
Importing React's taint APIs (`experimental_taintObjectReference` etc.) without `experimental.taint: true` is now a compile error instead of failing at runtime.
`javascript:` URLs are rejected by `router.push`/`replace`, `redirect()` and related Next.js navigation APIs, which previously passed them through.
Turbopack now infers module side effects by default (`experimental.turbopackInferModuleSideEffects`), so imports it determines to be side-effect free can be dropped from bundles.
An outer `'use cache'` that nests a short-lived cache now must declare an explicit `cacheLife`; previously the default profile was silently used.
The dev server now blocks cross-origin requests to internal assets from origins not listed in `allowedDevOrigins`, where it previously only warned.
The tsconfig settings Next.js writes and checks no longer rely on `baseUrl` or `moduleResolution: "node"` (deprecated in TypeScript 6); `paths` now resolve without `baseUrl`.
On the 15.5 line, Next.js now refuses to run with TypeScript >= 7.0 and exits with an error (the 16.x line gained TypeScript 7 support instead).
The Edge runtime (`export const runtime = 'edge'`) and the `preferredRegion` route segment config are deprecated with build warnings and `@deprecated` types; the Node.js runtime is the path forward.
Turbopack filesystem caching for `next build` (`experimental.turbopackFileSystemCacheForBuild`) is now on by default, so repeat builds reuse artifacts from `.next/cache`.
`experimental.prefetchInlining` is on by default: small segment prefetches are bundled into one response per link instead of one request per segment.
`experimental.optimisticRouting` (client-side route prediction) is on by default, changing when navigations commit and which segments are fetched.

`experimental.validateRSCRequestHeaders` is on by default: an RSC request whose headers do not match the client's cache-busting search parameter is no longer served as an RSC response (previously only validated when opted in).

The reworked App Router scroll and focus handling (`experimental.appNewScrollHandler`) is on by default: after navigation the active element is blurred instead of focusing the first focusable element in the segment.
`experimental.turbopackTreeShaking` is renamed to `experimental.turbopackModuleFragments`.
Removed config keys: `experimental.turbopackMemoryLimit` and `experimental.viewTransition` (view transitions work without a flag).
Requests to unknown paths whose `Sec-Fetch-Dest` is not a document (images, workers, manifest icons) now get a plain-text 404 instead of rendering the HTML not-found page.
`next build` type-checks with the project's TypeScript CLI by default (`experimental.useTypeScriptCli`, opt out with `false`) instead of the compiler API.

Undocumented methods on the custom-server `next()` instance (`setAssetPrefix()`, `revalidate()`, logging helpers and the legacy `render*` helpers) are deprecated with warnings; use `getRequestHandler()`.
The `opengraph-image` (and sibling image route) default export's return type is narrowed to `Response`; the other return types the types previously allowed failed the build.

`experimental.strictRouteMatching` is on by default: App Router URLs that cannot build a complete route tree are rejected, unreachable pages and incompatible parallel-route slots are reported, and interception routes need a canonical route; `deprecated.looseRouteMatching: true` is the escape hatch.
Pages Router support for React 18 is deprecated: `next dev`/`next build` warn when React 18 is installed, ahead of removal in 17.
`useReportWebVitals` moves to web-vitals v6: the FID metric is no longer reported and CLS/INP/LCP are now also reported for soft navigations with a `navigationURL`.

Client-side-rendering bailouts (`useSearchParams` without Suspense, resumed-render and CSR bailouts) now use React's `ReactDOM.browser` mechanism by default instead of throwing the Next.js bailout errors.
Unrecognized Server Action IDs now return 400 (malformed) or 409 (unknown in this deployment) for both fetch and MPA form submissions, instead of 404 or 500.
Turbopack now emits its runtime as one chunk shared across routes (`experimental.turbopackSharedRuntime` on by default) instead of a per-route runtime.
Turbopack production builds now mangle internal export names by default (`experimental.turbopackMangleExportNames`), shortening the names used to connect modules.
Turbopack production builds now generate shorter CSS Module class names (development keeps the long readable names).
